newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom says intends action in Regent Fund row.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom says intends action in Regent Fund row.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom said on Friday a plan by Regent Gaz Investment Company Limited to open an internationally traded fund backed by domestic Gazprom shares was contrary to the intentions of the Gazprom charter.

"The Management Committee intends to take action to enforce the principle of separate markets for domestic and international shares in the interests of RAO Gazprom and shareholders," it said in a statement.
Gazprom did not say what actions it would take and did not specifically say it would move to block the Regent fund.
"The Management Committee considers it its duty to warn investors of the high degree of risk associated with investing in Regent fund shares and other similar instruments," it said.
It quoted Regent's January 29 offering memorandum as saying the fund's success depended on restrictions in Gazprom's charter not prohibiting the fund from being implemented.

"Gazprom's Management Committee does indeed view the Regent fund's proposals as being contrary to the intentions of RAO Gazprom's Charter and the principle of the separation of the domestic and international markets for RAO Gazprom's shares," it said.
Gazprom in October 1996 launched an American Depositary Receipt (ADS) which allows international trading in Gazprom but trades at a price about four times that of underlying shares traded in Russia.
The premium is based largely on the difficulty of buying and trading local shares in the world's largest natural gas company.

Traders said that the $200 million fund, approximately one-third the size of the Gazprom ADS market, could weaken the price of the ADS and hurt prospects for the price of future international offerings of Gazprom shares.
It could also set a precedent among funds, they said.
Gazprom on Tuesday said it had asked the Cayman Islands-based Regent Gaz to suspend placing paper backed by Gazprom shares until Gazprom lawyers had reviewed the plan.

Gazprom reserves the right in its charter to approve all purchases of its shares by foreigners but the charter allows dealers to sell shares to any Russian entity after Gazprom waives its right to buy.
Traders say that as a result a number of foreign companies have set up wholly owned Russian subsidiaries which buy and hold Gazprom shares on their behalf and meet Russian legal restrictions.

They said the Regent Gaz fund, to be managed by Regent Fund Management in Hong Kong, part of the Regent Pacific Group which also has a Moscow subsidiary, Regent European Securities, was apparently the only international fund of Russian Gazprom stock.

At 1550 GMT, the Gazprom ADS, which covers 10 underlying shares, had eased to $19.400 from $19.475 at Thursday's close. Gazprom shares on the Russian Trading System in Moscow had eased to $0.474 from $0.490 at the previous close.
